summary: Forest Service lookout on Matney Knob, planned in 1933 and completed about 1935, with keepers named to 1946; a cell and radio tower now stands on the hill.

facts.design: Four-legged steel structure about 100 ft (30.5 m) high, painted aluminum (1953 federal survey description)
facts.status_note: No source read says whether the lookout cab is still on the summit; a trail guide describes a cell and radio tower on the hill.
facts.agency: State Forestry Commission / Ozark National Forest

access.note: Hiking-only trail; no source read closes the knob

visit.trail_note: Hiking trail only, no ATV or horse use on the stretch from point 41 to the Matney Knob trailhead (point 42)

events.note: National Ozark Forest contracted to buy 1,750 acres on the knob; a road and lookout tower were planned
Tower keeper Mayford Huffines named in a December 1934 item
Completed a few months before a September 1935 item; the year is approximate
Huffines, keeper for two years, moved to the Devil's Knob tower; successor not named
Mr. Vickers and family moved to the tower in May 1946
U.S. Coast and Geodetic Survey described the tower as a steel structure about 100 ft high

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The transcriptions spell the keeper's name Huffines, Husffines and Huggines; the 1935 and 1938 items both use Huffines, which the story follows.

sources.title: NGS datasheet GF0672, Matney Lookout Tower

notes_for_editor: The cab's fate is unknown: no source read says whether the lookout cab survives, and the cell and radio tower may postdate it. The trail guide (point 40) is undated. The 1946 item places the tower '20 miles north of Big Flat', which does not fit the Norfork location, so the story does not use that distance. The record's 30.5 m height matches the 1953 NGS description. The NGS datasheet has no condition entry after 1953.
